title: Hawaii under hurricane warning as Tropical Storm Lala approaches Big Island
dek: Tropical Storm Lala is moving toward Hawaii with hurricane conditions forecast to reach the Big Island by Saturday. A hurricane warning is in effect for the Big Island, with tropical storm warnings covering Maui County, Oahu, and Kauai County. Forecasters warn of up to 25 inches of rain, 3-foot storm surge, and life-threatening flooding.
author: The GoCheckMyNews Desk
key_fact: Hurricane conditions are expected to hit Hawaii's Big Island by Saturday, marking the first hurricane landfall threat to the state in over three decades.
bottom_line: Hurricane conditions are forecast to reach the Big Island Saturday, with the storm center expected to move near South Point and then south of the smaller islands Sunday. The actual impact will depend on whether Lala's center remains south of the islands as forecast, a detail officials acknowledged remains uncertain.
body: A hurricane warning is in effect for Hawaii's Big Island as Tropical Storm Lala approaches with hurricane conditions forecast to arrive by Saturday, according to CBS News reporting. The National Hurricane Center has also issued tropical storm warnings for Maui County, Oahu, and Kauai County, with tropical storm conditions possible across Oahu and Kauai County by Sunday morning.

As of Friday evening local time, Lala was located about 235 miles east-southeast of South Point on the Big Island and 440 miles southeast of Honolulu, according to the hurricane center's latest advisory reported by CBS News. The storm was moving west-northwest at 12 mph with maximum sustained winds of 65 mph. A tropical storm becomes a hurricane when maximum sustained winds reach 74 mph.

Forecasters warn of potentially severe rainfall and flooding. The National Hurricane Center said Lala is expected to produce rainfall totals of 8 to 12 inches across Maui and the Big Island, with maximum totals of 25 inches possible across the Big Island, according to CBS News reporting. Other islands could see 4 to 6 inches with maximum amounts of 8 inches. The center warned that this rainfall may produce life-threatening flooding and mudslides, especially in areas of steep terrain. Lala could also produce a storm surge as high as 3 feet along the coast, along with large waves and life-threatening rip current conditions.

Gov. Josh Green declared a state of emergency Thursday in anticipation of Lala's arrival. His proclamation activated potential disaster relief funds and directed all state agencies and officers to cooperate and extend services, materials, and facilities to assist in emergency response efforts, per CBS News. In a Friday night news briefing, Green cautioned residents and visitors to prepare for heavy flooding and the possibility of major power outages. He acknowledged uncertainty about the exact track, stating that the state was hoping Lala would be sufficiently far south so Hawaii would get just the periphery of the storm, but noted: "No promises, we've seen storms turn."

National Weather Service warning coordination meteorologist John Bravender noted that even though the forecast track shows the storm passing south of the islands, tropical storm force winds will extend north and could impact all the islands, according to CBS News. The Miami-based hurricane center warned that wind speeds could be significantly higher in elevated areas and on the windward sides of slopes and mountains.

Hawaii County Mayor Kimo Alameda told CBS News Friday morning that the greatest threats from the storm will vary by location: high surf for those close to the shoreline, high winds in different areas, and flooding concerns. He characterized the storm as potentially significant, saying "This could look like a big one."

The last hurricane to make landfall in Hawaii was Hurricane Iniki in 1992, which struck as a powerful Category 4 and was responsible for six deaths and $3 billion in damage, according to Gov. Green. The National Park Service announced that most areas of Volcanoes National Park on the Big Island would close to visitors by Friday afternoon ahead of the storm's arrival.
